omissionsFound.reason: Authenticated per-user server-sent events deliver bootstrap/runtime/state updates and must terminate with request/session lifecycle.
Create/rename/delete/add/remove are independent authenticated user-workspace mutations, separate from canonical desk-membership invariants.
Selected scope/watchlist/ticker is persisted per user and must not leak between users.
Authenticated live-priority hints can influence allocation priority but cannot bypass the canonical subscription manager or permanent GLD/SLV/USO pins.
Export excludes API keys, forces Demo/autostart-off; import restores only the authenticated workspace and preserves current Data Mode.
Desktop external-link action accepts only valid http/https URLs and dispatches via platform-specific safe launcher.
Privileged quit stops engine, terminates the app window, closes the server and exits in a bounded sequence.
Privileged provider-test action must use configured/persisted credentials without leaking or changing admission/routing authority.
Clear/refresh actions have different authority and must not bypass canonical persistence/freshness/recovery behavior.
Targeted VIX/global/capability/stream/data-engine refresh actions are user/admin triggers into existing canonical owners, not alternative acquisition logic.
Manual maintenance/integrity reports validate profile/watchlist/cache/runtime/feed/build state without destructive repair or hidden resets.
Privileged engine/Data Mode control is distinct from start/stop and must preserve Demo/Live boundaries and credentials.
Authenticated community evidence ingestion is contextual/corroborative only and must retain provenance/materiality boundaries.
Official completed-session TAIEX close is distinct from Twelve Data live/direct state and ETF proxy fallback.
HTTP latency/in-flight/slow-interactive and hosted quota counters are runtime diagnostics, not product intelligence.

Current v18 portability contract requires renderer behavior across Chrome and WebKit in addition to packaged macOS/Windows runtime proof; the canonical Qualified workflow binds Chrome behavior, WebKit compatibility and documentation-owner browser evidence to this responsibility.

notes: Do not interpret runtimeMode hosted foundation or hosted request telemetry as v19 hosted-product activation; v19 remains blocked by #113.
Manual refresh/operator actions must delegate to existing canonical owners and are audited for direct-route role parity in T6.
